rationale.why: The Inventory component is the SINGLE public entry point for an app. It receives providers + steps + layout config, composes the runtime, and renders the shell. Apps NEVER compose providers manually or import StepRouter/SlotSystem directly.

composition-order.step: Validate providers (no duplicate IDs, version compatibility)
Validate steps (unique route paths, registered guards)
Build Trie from step routes (O(P log P) once at mount)
Mount global slots from children (modals, toasts)
Call onReady() once all providers initialized

error-isolation.rule: Each Pattern wrapped in its own ErrorBoundary (via withErrorBoundary extension).
Each View wrapped in its own ErrorBoundary (declared in defineLayoutView/defineRenderView).
StepRouter wrapped in outer ErrorBoundary that calls onError().
Inventory wrapped in fatal ErrorBoundary that renders a static recovery page.
error-isolation.rationale: A single pattern crash does not bring down the View. A View crash does not bring down the app.

gates.gate: Apps never import composeProviders, ModuleRegistry, StepRouter directly.
Inventory props are validated against schemas at mount time.
Provider IDs are unique within an Inventory instance.
Step routes are unique within an Inventory instance.
Inventory shell has a *.inventory.test.tsx covering composition + error isolation.
Initial bundle of Inventory ≤ 180kb gzip (measured via size-limit).
Lighthouse Performance ≥ 90 on the default app shell.
